# Why Matsya is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *matsya*. This is the file on how **Matsya** replaced it.

The Matsya myth is India’s flood-saga: the warning, the ark, the world’s drowning, and the mooring at the one remaining peak — with the added theology of the avatāra, Vishnu descending to preserve both species and scripture. The telling grows from a brief Vedic episode to one of the Purāṇas’ most beloved complete narratives.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Matsya
- **ASCII form:** matsya
- **Meaning:** "'The Fish' — the first avatāra of Viṣṇu, who saved Manu and the Vedas from the great deluge"
- **Domain of influence:** Fish Avatar of Vishnu
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** मत्स्य
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 329 of 597

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/ˈmɑːtsyə/` — “MAHT-chyuh”

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Matsya** lives at [/matsya/](/matsya/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/matsya/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/matsya/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/matsya/patterns/).

aSCII-equivalent form

## Where the Name Stood First

Matsya rides the first panel of every daśāvatāra frieze — from the Gupta reliefs of Deogarh to the great sequence-walls of Angkor. The fish-torso Vishnu of the early medieval images is his monumental form. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** (the flood survived by ark — the species' resilience plan, executed by a fish.); **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** (the great fish that bore the ark through the deluge — the flood survived by boat is his myth.); **Insurance & Protection Services** (the one who insured the species — the ark against the deluge, the policy that paid out in full.). The [Resonance File](/matsya/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
